title: A closed subset of a fibre has a finite-type reduced closure model
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a finite type morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let $y\in Y$, and let $A\subseteq X_y$ be a closed subset of the scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. For each $t\in Y$ write $p_t:X_t\to X$ for the canonical projection. Set $D=\overline{p_y(A)}\subseteq X$, where the bar denotes topological closure. There are a reduced scheme $Z$ [def-pc-reduced-scheme] and a closed immersion $j:Z\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] with image $D$, such that $h=f\circ j:Z\to Y$ is of finite type. For every $t\in Y$ the canonical morphism of fibres $j_t:Z_t\to X_t$ is a homeomorphism onto the closed subspace $p_t^{-1}(D)$ of $X_t$. In particular $p_y^{-1}(D)=A$, so $j_y$ identifies the underlying space of $Z_y$ with $A$. These are assertions about underlying spaces; no reducedness of the scheme fibres $Z_t$ is asserted. The subset $A$ may be empty; no irreducibility, Noetherianity, separatedness, or flatness hypothesis on $X$, $Y$, or $f$ is imposed.

proof.text: Put $B=p_y(A)$ and $F=f^{-1}(\{y\})$. By the fibre homeomorphism in [def-pc-scheme-fibre], $B$ is closed in the subspace $F$. Thus $B=C\cap F$ for an ambient closed subset $C\subseteq X$. Since $C$ contains $B$, it contains $D=\overline B$; hence $B\subseteq D\cap F\subseteq C\cap F=B$. Applying the injective map $p_y$ gives $p_y^{-1}(D)=A$.

source.place: Discussion immediately preceding Tag 054Y (lemma-cover-generic-fibre-neighbourhood); fibre topology is Tag 01K1 (schemes-lemma-fibre-topological)

proof.text: The subset $D$ is closed by definition of closure. Apply clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] with $T=D$. It supplies the reduced induced closed subscheme $Z=D_{\mathrm{red}}$ and a closed immersion $j:Z\hookrightarrow X$ with image exactly $D$.

Clause (a) of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper] says in particular that the closed immersion $j$ is of finite type. Since $f$ is of finite type by hypothesis, clause (1) of [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change] applies to $Z\xrightarrow{j}X\xrightarrow{f}Y$ and gives that $h=f\circ j$ is of finite type.

Fix any $t\in Y$ and let $q_t:Z_t\to Z$ be the fibre projection for $h$. The fibre-product definition [def-pc-scheme-fibre] gives the canonical $j_t:Z_t\to X_t$ with $p_tj_t=jq_t$, using the maps $jq_t$ and $Z_t\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$. The same cited node identifies $|Z_t|$ with $h^{-1}(t)$ and $|X_t|$ with $f^{-1}(t)$. By [def-weil-closed-immersion], $j$ is a homeomorphism onto $D$; its restriction is therefore a homeomorphism $h^{-1}(t)\simeq D\cap f^{-1}(t)$. Conjugating this restriction by the two fibre homeomorphisms gives a homeomorphism $|Z_t|\simeq p_t^{-1}(D)$. The equation $p_tj_t=jq_t$ and injectivity of $p_t$ identify this map with $j_t$ itself. The target subspace is closed because $D$ is closed and $p_t$ is continuous. For $t=y$, Step 1 identifies it with $A$.

lean.statement: theorem exists_reduced_closed_fiber_model {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] (y : Y) (A : Set (f.fiber y)) (hA : IsClosed A) : ∃ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (j : Z ⟶ X), IsReduced Z ∧ IsClosedImmersion j ∧ Set.range j = closure ((f.fiberι y) '' A) ∧ LocallyOfFiniteType (j ≫ f) ∧ QuasiCompact (j ≫ f) ∧ (∀ t : Y, Topology.IsClosedEmbedding (fiberMap (a := j ≫ f) (b := f) j rfl (Y.fromSpecResidueField t)) ∧ Set.range (fiberMap (a := j ≫ f) (b := f) j rfl (Y.fromSpecResidueField t)) = (f.fiberι t) ⁻¹' closure ((f.fiberι y) '' A)) ∧ (f.fiberι y) ⁻¹' closure ((f.fiberι y) '' A) = A
